receipt.public_excerpt: The last known transit of Venus was in 1882.

evidence_items.explanation: The recorded responses to ordinary questions about the gravitational constant and Venus transits contain numerous factual errors, including false biographies, mission history, and transit dates. Additional invented-paradox prompts produce fabricated explanations, although those prompts provide weaker evidence about ordinary use.

The developers report 26% MC1 accuracy for the 120B model on TruthfulQA, while acknowledging low absolute performance. This corroborates reliability concerns but measures a specific benchmark, not the frequency of fabricated statements in public-demo responses; the exact testing dates are unspecified.

The paper reports useful scientific capabilities, including 77.6% on PubMedQA and 68.2% on LaTeX equation probes. These successes constrain any suggestion that Galactica was uniformly wrong, but do not contradict recurring fabrication.
